Vigor

/VIG-or/ — rhymes with trigger · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Vigor is physical strength and energetic force.

After a good night's sleep, she attacked the project with renewed vigor.

Worked Example

The young athlete bounded up the stadium steps two at a time, her vigor evident in every powerful leap.

Vigor captures both the physical strength and the energetic force in action. A plain word like 'strength' misses the dynamic, driving quality; 'energy' alone misses the physical power. Vigor names the combination precisely.

How Vigor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

strength

strength: physical power of body or muscles

energy

energy: capacity for lively activity and effort

vitality

vitality: flourishing life-force and lively spirit

Antonyms

lethargy

lethargy: sluggish drowsiness that drains all energy

feebleness

feebleness: frail weakness lacking force or power

How Strong Is It? — lethargy → strength → stamina → vigor

lethargy vs. vigor

lethargy vs. vigor: Lethargy is the opposite end of the scale from vigor: lethargy is heavy, sluggish drowsiness, while vigor is bursting, energetic force.

strength vs. vigor

strength vs. vigor: Strength is weaker on this scale than vigor: strength is raw physical power, while vigor adds the lively, driving energy to put that power to work.

stamina vs. vigor

stamina vs. vigor: Stamina comes close to vigor but stops short: stamina lets you keep going for a long time, while vigor is the fresh, forceful energy you attack a task with.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vig

Root — vig: to be lively, flourish (from vigere) (Latin)

Suffix — -or

Suffix — -or: state or quality (noun-forming) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Vigor is built on Latin vigere, 'to be lively and flourish,' plus the noun ending -or: literally 'the state of being lively' — energetic physical strength and force.

Use the root in a new word: invigorate

Use the root in a new word: invigorate: A cold morning swim will invigorate you — literally put vigor into you, filling you with lively strength and energy.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Vigor captures both physical strength and dynamic energy — use it when describing active, forceful effort or movement. For just physical power, 'strength' is simpler; for just liveliness, 'energy' works better.
